**The rubric -- 5 dimensions, written BEFORE looking at any image.** Mike named layout, contrast, density, typography; `hierarchy` earns the fifth slot because it is the single thing that most separates a 60 from a 90 and no other axis covers it (a page can have good type, fine contrast, right density and still be a flat undifferentiated wall). `polish` was considered and REJECTED -- it overlaps all five and becomes a fudge factor. 5 axes, not 12 (RULE#18). (1) **layout** -- structure, alignment to a visible grid, grouping, whether the 1280 gets used or left as gutters. (2) **typography** -- type scale, measure/line-length, leading, whether heading levels out-rank their body. (3) **contrast** -- legibility of text on its ground, whether emphasis actually reads, anything washed out or harsh. (4) **density** -- information per screen; cramped jumble vs empty stage; is the whitespace grouping or just padding. (5) **hierarchy** -- can you tell what this page IS and where to look first, in one second; does the eye have a path. Plus **overall** -- a holistic judgement of how the page looks, informed by the five but NOT their mean.

**The anchors.** **30 = unfinished.** You would not show it. Elements visibly misalign or collide; a wall of undifferentiated text, or scattered boxes on no grid; one type size doing every job; text you squint at; either a cramped jumble or ~70% empty screen with a strip of content in it. No path for the eye -- you cannot say what the page is for in three seconds. **60 = competent, undesigned.** Nothing is broken. A consistent grid and a readable type scale exist. But something obvious holds it back: dead space where content should be, a heading that does not out-rank its body, a measure running long, uniform grey where emphasis is needed, or a layout ignoring half the width. Reads as a developer's page -- functional, not designed. **90 = designed.** Clear first read: you know what the page is and where to look within a second. Deliberate alignment, whitespace that groups rather than pads, a type scale with real contrast between levels, comfortable measure, one or two accents doing work, the full 1280 used without stretching prose to it. Only nits remain. Extremes: <=20 = actually broken (overlap, error state); >=95 = nothing I would change; 100 is not awarded.

assign.now: Baseline scored (all 18). Math tiers correlated -- taste wins decisively. Cheap tiers running.

log.msg: **THE TIEBREAK, n=18 at 1280. TASTE WINS, decisively.** | tier | MAE | RMSE | bias | Spearman | Pearson | mean | range | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **taste** | **7.22** | **11.14** | **-1.33** | **+0.266** | **+0.134** | 68.9 | 49-91 | | math (findings) | 12.78 | 16.62 | **+11.67** | -0.039 | **-0.393** | 81.9 | 70-96 | | *my baseline* | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | 70.2 | 44-80 | Taste is closer on every measure. The damning number is math's **Pearson -0.393**: its score is ANTI-correlated with how a page looks, so as a predictor of visual quality it is worse than a constant 70 would be. Taste and math agree with each other only 0.501 Spearman / 13.0 MAE -- they were never measuring the same thing.

**WHY math is anti-correlated: it is a findings COUNTER, and findings scale with content.** math score vs its own findings count: Pearson **-0.709**. Findings count vs DOM node count: **+0.633**. Therefore math score vs node count: Pearson -0.270, **Spearman -0.519**. My baseline vs node count: +0.14 Pearson / +0.10 Spearman -- i.e. how much is on a page has NO bearing on how good it looks, and math thinks it has a strong negative one. **The math tier rewards emptiness.** Its three most-overrated pages are the three emptiest in the corpus (/web/layout/flow/ +52 at 149 nodes, /web/nav/sidebar/ +18, /notes/git-branch-names/ +18 at 40 nodes); its ONE underrated page is the densest and best-designed (/framework/ -10 at 626 nodes). An empty page trips no rules, and absence of findings is not presence of design. This is a rule-level defect, not eighteen page-level ones (RULE#18).

**Math's floor is 70.** Across 18 pages spanning a real 44-80 in appearance, findings.json never emits below 70 and never above 96 -- a 26-point range, compressed at the top, describing a 36-point reality. A tier that cannot say 'below 70' cannot flag a page as bad, which is the only thing a design metric is for. Taste spans 49-91 and its bias is -1.33, i.e. its LEVEL is right; its problem is ordering, not scale.

**CALIBRATION BUG #1 -- `width-used` is implemented twice and both are wrong. This is the highest-value fix in the set.** It is the prime objective as a number, weight 8/62 in taste. Same 18 pages, same 1280, the two tiers' readings (taste %, math %): /framework/ 10 vs 71 | LayoutTool/tests 6 vs 74 | web/nav/sidebar 6 vs 90 | ext/toc 7 vs 61 | ui/panel 6 vs 76 | ui/tags 6 vs 76 | **web/layout/flow 7 vs 208** | core/Page 7 vs 54 | ext/layout 7 vs 74 | web/nav/wall 6 vs 85 | theme/lew42 7 vs 69 | **web/nav/crumbs 6 vs 149** | overview/children 6 vs 74 | audit 7 vs 74 | Page/nav 7 vs 69 | styles/util 10 vs 69 | **git-branch-names null vs 61** | framework/ai 27 vs 70. **taste reads 6-10% for SEVENTEEN of eighteen pages** -- its ok floor is 0.28, so every page in the corpus scores a hard ZERO on that band and taste silently forfeits 13% of its total weight uniformly. It is a dead band, not a discriminator. **math reads >100% on two pages** (208.3% and 148.5%) -- content span cannot exceed the width it was given; both offenders are pages with CSS-transform-scaled previews in the rail, so untransformed geometry is being summed. Eyeballed truth for those pages is ~45% and ~65%.

**CALIBRATION BUG #2 -- /web/layout/flow/ scores 96 (grade A) and is the worst-looking page in the corpus at 44.** A 52-point error, the largest single miss by either tier. What the image shows and neither tier caught: the h1 sits at x=400 while the content it heads starts at x=614 (a 214px orphaned title); the band x=330-614 is empty for the full 800px height; and below the rail's framed preview, two blocks of scaled demo text sit ON THE PAGE GROUND with no card, no border, no label, at two DIFFERENT left offsets (x=64 and x=118), in ~8px teal on grey. Math fired 3 low findings: two `pad-scale` and one `hierarchy`. It owns a `heading-offset` rule -- 'A heading doesn't line up with its own text' -- which did NOT fire on a 214px offset here, while firing TWICE on /framework/, whose only misalignment is prose wrapping at 1026 against cards ending at 1074. **The rule is firing on the wrong pages.** Root cause is likely shared with bug #1: scale-transformed previews report untransformed geometry, so flow's rail reads as full-width content and its offsets read as aligned.

**CALIBRATION BUG #3 -- /framework/ is the best-looking page in the corpus (80) and taste scores it 49, its worst.** Taste zeroes five of eleven bands, and FOUR of the five are artifacts of measuring an app shell rather than faults of the design. `measure` = 26.1 chars, credit 0 (weight 10, the heaviest band) -- the actual prose measure is ~100 chars; the reading is being dragged under the 34-char floor by 14 sidebar nav labels and 5 stat-card captions. `contrast` = 8.38, credit 0 -- that is a 48px h1 over a MEDIAN that includes 10-11px chrome microtype; against its own body text the ratio is ~3.0, dead centre of the 2.2-4.2 ideal. `repetition` = 0.96, credit 0 -- 96% of text sits in identically-classed sibling groups because the page IS a nav rail plus a five-card stat row, which is correct design being charged as a wall. `width-used` = 0.1, credit 0 -- bug #1. Only `scale` (13 gap sizes) is a fair charge. Net: 31 of 62 weight forfeited, ~27 of it wrongly. **Fix: measure prose bands over PROSE, and take `contrast` and `measure` against body text, not against everything with a font-size.**

**CALIBRATION BUG #4 -- both tiers crown /notes/git-branch-names/ (taste 91, math 96); I score it 78.** It IS the cleanest setting in the corpus -- nothing broken, one left edge, the best contrast, column-aligned `#` comments in the code block. But its content column ends at x=833, so **447px (35%) of the 1280 is empty grey**, and it carries no navigation whatsoever, so the page is unmoored from the site. That is the prime objective's exact prohibition -- widescreen space gets USED, not left as gutter -- and neither tier charges a point for it, because taste's width-used band returns null here (no reading at all) and math's returns 61% and fires nothing. Bug #1 again, in its third form. Secondary nit neither tier can see: the h2 `Why <name>/<branch>?` renders a code chip at display size, so a 264px black bar dwarfs the words around it.

**METHOD WARNING, and it changes how every number here must be read: MAE ALONE IS A TRAP.** My baseline has mean 70.2, sd 7.98. A predictor that ignores the image entirely and returns **a constant 72** scores **MAE 5.22** -- beating taste (7.22) and crushing math (12.78). So ranking scorers by mean absolute error alone concludes that the best visual-design metric on this site is the number 72, which is absurd. **A candidate must clear two bars, not one: spread comparable to the baseline's sd ~8, AND rank correlation.** Spreads: my baseline sd 7.98 | taste sd 8.81 | math sd 6.15 | haiku sd **1.65** | constant sd 0. Reporting MAE without sd is how a useless scorer gets adopted.

**HAIKU: cheap, fast, and it is a constant predictor. Do not use it.** 18/18 images scored, 19 turns, 112s wall, **$0.188 total = $0.0105/image**, 99,503 tokens = **5,528 tokens/image** (624 output). Headline agreement looks GOOD -- MAE **5.06**, bias +0.83, Pearson 0.438 -- and it is a mirage: its scores span **[68, 72]**, sd 1.65, against a reality of 44-80. It barely beats the constant-72 control (5.22). Spearman **0.207** = noise. **14 of 18 rows carry two or fewer distinct values across the five dimensions** -- it picks one number per page and copies it into every axis, which is the signature of a model not actually discriminating. On /web/layout/flow/ (my 44, the worst page) it said 72 and wrote 'division leaves right-side whitespace creating asymmetric composition' -- it saw whitespace and called it composition, missing the orphaned h1, the unframed escaped previews and the 8px illegible text. Per-dimension MAE 5.0-8.1 with spearman 0.07-0.38. **Verdict: Haiku cannot carry this work at any price.**

assign.now: Writing up the agreement table and the verdict.

log.msg: **SONNET IS THE RESULT: it ranks pages better than BOTH of the site's mathematical tiers, at 3.5 cents an image.** 18/18 scored, 19 turns, 305s wall, **$0.623 total = $0.0346/image**, 101,166 tokens = **5,620 tokens/image** (932 output). MAE **6.44**, bias -4.00, **Spearman +0.625**, Pearson 0.540. At n=18 the critical |rho| is ~0.475 (p=0.05) and ~0.60 (p=0.01), so **Sonnet's ordering is the ONLY candidate here that is statistically significant** -- taste (+0.266), Haiku (+0.207) and math (-0.039) all sit inside noise. Only **2 of 18** rows are flat, i.e. it really is scoring five separate axes. Its one weakness is COMPRESSION: sd 3.91 against my 7.98, range [60,72], so it hedges toward the middle and under-called /web/layout/flow/ at 62 where I said 44. A monotone affine rescale -- `70.2 + (s - 66.2) * 2.04` -- fixes level and spread (MAE 6.13, sd 7.98) and leaves the rank correlation untouched at 0.625. Per-dimension Spearman: **density +0.790** (the single strongest signal found anywhere in this study), hierarchy +0.425, layout +0.414, typography +0.351, contrast +0.335. Its prose is real too -- 780 chars/image, and on flow it independently spotted 'an annotation block that is visually disconnected from the card above it', which is the escaped-preview defect.

**THE FULL AGREEMENT TABLE (deliverable 2).** | tier | MAE | bias | sd | Spearman | Pearson | $/image | tokens/image | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | *my baseline (opus-5)* | -- | -- | **7.98** | -- | -- | -- | ~4.5k in | | **sonnet-5** | 6.44 | -4.00 | 3.91 | **+0.625** | +0.540 | $0.0346 | 5,620 | | haiku-5 | 5.06 | +0.83 | **1.65** | +0.207 | +0.438 | $0.0105 | 5,528 | | taste.json | 7.22 | -1.33 | 8.81 | +0.266 | +0.134 | $0 | 0 | | findings.json (math) | 12.78 | **+11.67** | 6.15 | -0.039 | **-0.393** | $0 | 0 | | *constant 72 (control)* | 5.22 | +1.80 | **0** | n/a | n/a | $0 | 0 | Read the sd column before the MAE column: Haiku and the constant control 'win' MAE by refusing to discriminate. Ranked by usefulness: **sonnet > taste > haiku ~ constant > math**.

**Per-page, every tier, sorted by how the page actually looks (me | sonnet | haiku | taste | math):** 44 | 62 | 68 | 67 | 96 | /web/layout/flow/ -- 63 | 62 | 72 | 63 | 77 | /framework/ext/toc/ -- 64 | 60 | 68 | 60 | 82 | /web/nav/sidebar/ -- 65 | 67 | 72 | 65 | 81 | /framework/ui/tags/ -- 68 | 70 | 72 | 64 | 83 | /framework/ui/panel/ -- 68 | 60 | 72 | 71 | 76 | /framework/styles/layers/theme/lew42/ -- 70 | 66 | 68 | 72 | 83 | /web/nav/crumbs/ -- 71 | 60 | 72 | 69 | 81 | /framework/core/Page/ -- 72 | 63 | 72 | 74 | 79 | /framework/core/Page/overview/children/ -- 72 | 70 | 72 | 76 | 84 | /framework/core/Page/nav/ -- 72 | 67 | 72 | 78 | 83 | /framework/styles/layers/util/ -- 72 | 70 | 72 | 70 | 82 | /framework/ai/ -- 74 | 72 | 72 | 69 | 74 | /framework/ext/layout/ -- 75 | 67 | 68 | 70 | 83 | /web/nav/wall/ -- 77 | 70 | 72 | 57 | 81 | /framework/ext/LayoutTool/tests/ -- 78 | 68 | 71 | 91 | 96 | /notes/git-branch-names/ -- 79 | 68 | 72 | 75 | 83 | /framework/audit/ -- 80 | 70 | 72 | 49 | 70 | /framework/. Note the two right-hand columns move OPPOSITE to the left one at both ends: math's best page is my worst, and taste's worst page is my best.

**Taste is salvageable and math is not, and the numbers say so specifically.** Drop taste's two dense-page outliers (/framework/ -31 and /framework/ext/LayoutTool/tests/ -20, the two densest pages in the corpus at 626 and 1,696 nodes) and the remaining 16 give **MAE 4.94, Spearman +0.724** -- better than Sonnet. Math on the same 16 gives MAE 13.50, Spearman +0.185, Pearson -0.293, i.e. removing the flow outlier does not help it at all, because its defect is systemic rather than two bad pages. **So taste is a working instrument with two identifiable failure modes (both 'this page has a lot on it'), and math is not an instrument for this question.** Fix order: (1) `width-used` in BOTH tiers -- bug #1, it is the prime objective as a number and it is dead in taste and >100% in math; (2) measure `measure` and `contrast` over PROSE only, not over chrome microtype -- bug #3; (3) stop `heading-offset` firing on the wrong pages -- bug #2; (4) give math a floor below 70, or accept that it ranks cleanliness rather than quality.

**THE VERDICT, in two sentences (deliverable 3).** **`taste.json` is closer to how pages actually look** -- MAE 7.22 against my baseline versus math's 12.78, and math's score is *anti*-correlated with appearance (Pearson **-0.393**), because it counts findings and findings scale with content, so it systematically rewards emptiness: it hands grade A / 96 to /web/layout/flow/, the worst-looking page in the corpus at 44, and gives its single lowest score to /framework/, the best-looking at 80. **A cheaper model CAN carry this work, but only Sonnet** -- at $0.035 and 5,620 tokens per image it is the only candidate whose ORDERING is statistically significant (Spearman +0.625, p<0.01) and it out-ranks both of the site's mathematical tiers, needing just the monotone rescale `70.2 + (s - 66.2) * 2.04` to fix its habit of hedging into the 60-72 band; Haiku at a third the price is a constant-70 generator (sd 1.65, 14 of 18 rows flat) and must not be used.

**What I did NOT reach, stated plainly (no silent truncation).** (a) The optional 'Fable + hard metrics doubly honed' experiment was NOT run as a pipeline -- but I did pull the frozen metrics for the pages my scores felt least stable on, and the answer is a clear yes: the numbers sharpened the judgement decisively and produced calibration bugs #1 and #3, which pure vision would have called 'looks a bit empty' instead of 'width-used reads 6-10% on seventeen of eighteen pages'. **Recommendation: pair vision with the metrics, and use vision to AUDIT the metric rather than the page.** (b) Only `overall` was compared for the math tiers, because neither taste.json nor findings.json emits per-dimension scores -- the five-axis comparison exists only for the model tiers. (c) Single-scorer baseline: no self-consistency re-run, so my own repeatability is unmeasured; the honest caveat is that a second pass by me would likely move individual pages a few points, though not the two 30+ point findings. (d) 18 pages is a small n -- Spearman needs |rho|>0.475 for p=0.05 here, which is why I report significance rather than just the coefficient.

**Instrument note, and it cuts against my own numbers (memory: 'instruments find themselves first').** Two of the five rubric axes were harder to score than the other three, and it shows in the cross-model data: `contrast` has the WORST agreement of any dimension for both cheap tiers (Sonnet MAE 9.00, Haiku 8.11) and `hierarchy` the second worst (9.33 / 7.67), while `density` is the best (Sonnet Spearman +0.790). I suspect `contrast` is doing two jobs -- literal text-on-ground legibility AND whether the emphasis SYSTEM reads -- and should be split or renamed before this rubric is used at scale. `density` is the axis to trust and to automate first. Do not retune anything off this single run.

assign.outcome: **taste.json is the tier that matches how pages look; findings.json is anti-correlated with it (Pearson -0.393) and must not be used to rank design.** Baseline landed at `ai/2026-08-17/vision-baseline/baseline.json` -- 18 frozen 1280x800 shots, content-hashed, five anchored dimensions each with raw prose. Agreement: taste MAE 7.22 / Spearman +0.266; math MAE 12.78 / Spearman -0.039 / bias +11.7 with a hard floor of 70. Cheap tiers: **sonnet-5 is good enough at $0.035 and 5,620 tokens per image** (MAE 6.44, Spearman +0.625 -- the only significant ordering measured, and better than both math tiers); haiku-5 is a constant-70 generator (sd 1.65) and is not. Four calibration bugs named with the image as evidence, the top one shared by both tiers: **`width-used` reads 6-10% on seventeen of eighteen pages in taste (a dead band forfeiting 13% of its weight uniformly) and >100% on two pages in math** -- and it is the prime objective as a number. Root cause of the worst miss (/web/layout/flow/ scored 96 by math, 44 by me): CSS-transform-scaled previews report untransformed geometry.
